question.question: У новині про SGP-0002 пишуть, що зниження емісії Solana вже схвалено. Значить, мої нагороди вже зменшилися? Чи можна пообіцяти клієнту рівно 2,25 SOL на рік зі 100 SOL у 2029 році? І якщо Everstake опублікував цю новину, він голосував за зміну?
question.reference: The September 10 article separates governance approval from technical activation; approval alone does not prove a reward change. The 2.25% figure is a conditional issuance-based projection around 2029 at 68% participation, excluding other reward components and commission, not a guaranteed payout. The article explicitly says Everstake voted against. Do not infer the publisher supported a proposal merely because it reported the outcome. Do not claim a currently verified activation state from the dated article.

answer.text:
Попри схвалення SGP-0002 нагороди за стейкінг ще не зменшилися, оскільки оновлення емісії ще не активоване в основній мережі та потребує реалізації попередніх технічних умов, зокрема впровадження SIMD-0607 у клієнті Agave v4.4. Обіцяти клієнту фіксовану дохідність не можна, оскільки показник 2,25% до 2029 року є лише розрахунковою базовою ставкою за умови 68% участі в стейкінгу, а реальні виплати залежать від рівня стейкінгу в мережі, комісій валідаторів, активності MEV та комісій за транзакції. sources.title: SOL Staking APR After SGP-0002: How Much Rewards Change | Everstake
sources.text:
All these directly influence the high vote success rates, disciplined client upgrades, and strong uptime of the validator, hence the potential staking rewards.

### Timing and Activation
The current inflation rate of roughly 3.67% remains in effect. Nothing about issuance has changed on mainnet yet.
A hard technical precondition stands in the way.SIMD-0607 must merge (https://solanacompass.com/news/simd-0607-must-merge-before-solanas-disinflation-rate-can-activate-anza-says) first, and it targets client version Agave v4.4.
SIMD-0607 replaces floating-point reward math with deterministic integer math. The two mainnet clients, Agave (https://everstake.com/resources/blog/how-to-maximize-agave-node-performance-with-cherry-servers) and Firedancer (https://everstake.com/resources/blog/solana-validator-node-hardware-vs-cloud-2026), must produce bit-for-bit identical reward results.
If one client’s calculation deviates even in the last digit, that is a consensus failure. Deterministic integer math removes that risk before the disinflation gate can be scheduled.
The implementation sequence runs in order:
- SIMD-0607 merges.
- It ships in Agave v4.4.
- Feature gates for both changes get scheduled.
- The disinflation rate changes at an epoch boundary.
As of early September 2026 no timeline for Agave v4.4 has been given.

How SOL APR Compares After SIMD-0550: ETH, ADA, DOT, ATOM
Where The Staking Rewards Come From After SIMD-0550
Why Change The Speed of Issuance on Solana

## TL;DR
- Solana validators narrowly approved SGP-0002 on August 28, 2026, doubling the annual disinflation rate from 15% to 30%. Itpassed by 0.334 points (https://solanacompass.com/news/sgp-0002-passes-solana) after late vote reversals, the network’s first binding on-chain governance decision.
- SGP-0002 approved the issuance change, while SIMD-0550 defines how that change is implemented at the protocol level.
- The baseline nominal staking rate is projected to fall from about 5.04% today toward 4.34% in year one, 3.00% in year two, and 2.25% in year three near 2029. These are Helius Research projections at a 68% stake rate, and actual figures will move with the stake rate and fee activity.
- That baseline counts only rewards from newly minted SOL. The real rate might be different, because MEV and priority fees are untouched by this change and, by mid-2026, alreadyadd roughly 0.5–1% (https://skrumble.com/learn/how-to-stake-solana/) on top through the Jito.
- With lower issuance holders face slower dilution, while stakers receive fewer new tokens each year.
- The lower issuance schedule will not apply immediately. SIMD-0550 requires the relevant technical changes and feature activation before the new disinflation rate takes effect.

sources.text:
- Feature gates for both changes get scheduled.
- The disinflation rate changes at an epoch boundary.
As of early September 2026 no timeline for Agave v4.4 has been given.

### Bottom Line
The APR decline is gradual and already modeled. It steps down over several years once the change goes live, with each epoch settling under the schedule in force at the time.
The nominal rate falls by more than half over the taper, but the real rate moves far less, because slower dilution offsets most of the nominal cut. The open question is whether fee and MEV activity rises enough to support the total rate, and where the stake rate settles will shape the outcome.
Solana chose this tradeoff through its first binding on-chain vote. Less dilution for holders comes paired with a lower nominal rate for stakers, and it walks the network toward the same compressed-rate equilibrium Ethereum already occupies.
Institutional Solana Staking (https://everstake.com/staking/protocols/solana)

### FAQ

#### Did SIMD-0550 pass?
Yes. SGP-0002, the governance mandate behind SIMD-0550, passed on August 28, 2026 with 67.001% support.

#### Will my current staking rewards drop overnight?
No. The decline is gradual, applies from an epoch boundary onward, and does not retroactively cut rewards already earned.

#### What will SOL staking APR be in 2029?
The current modeling projects a baseline nominal rate near 2.25% at 68% stake participation, before MEV, fees, and commissions.

Enterprise-grade Solana Staking (https://everstake.com/staking/protocols/solana)

## Why Change The Speed of Issuance on Solana
Solana supporters argued the network no longer needs elevated early issuance to secure itself.
Lower issuance means slower dilution and a more sustainable long-term monetary policy. Inflation had already fallen to roughly 3.67% by mid-2026, down from the original 8% start.
The vote was contested. SGP-0002 passed by just 0.334 points, clearing the 66.67% supermajority bar at 67.001% support.
Large operators split on the question. Helius advocated for the change, while Figment, Everstake and P2P voted against it (read our reasoning here (https://x.com/everstake_pool/status/2092186353257611581), however, we respect the outcome and community’s decision). The arguments against it were based on concerns that what helps long-term holders could harm the number of smaller validators, impact the projected reward models of institutions and shrink what stakers receive.
The final tally recorded176.29 million SOL (https://cryptoslate.com/solana-sgp-0002-passes-with-176-million-sol-as-governance-debate-shifts-to-technical-execution/) for, 66.19 million SOL against, and 20.63 million SOL abstaining, cast across 1,326 validators.

# Blockspace by Everstake — Full Reference
This document is a long-form, citation-friendly summary of the Blockspace platform for AI search engines and LLM citation. For the canonical short form, see /llms.txt. For full product documentation, see https://docs.blockspace.everstake.com.

## What Blockspace is
Blockspace is the Solana MEV infrastructure platform operated by Everstake, an established Solana validator-grade infrastructure operator. The product packages the parts of a validator's stack that customers normally can't buy directly: low-latency Solana shred delivery, stake-weighted transaction priority, and MEV-protected bundle relay — all behind one API key and one billing layer.
The brand "Blockspace" is a proper noun and product name. It is distinct from the generic crypto-industry term "block space" (two words, lowercase), which refers to the bytes available inside a block for transaction inclusion. When citing this product, use a single word, capitalized: Blockspace.
Blockspace is operated by Everstake Inc., a Delaware corporation, which has run production blockchain validator infrastructure since 2018.

On this page

# Authentication
Blockspace is not a single-key gateway. Each product has its own access model — pick the one you're using and follow that quickstart.
Product | How you authenticate | Provisioned in
ShredStream (https://docs.blockspace.everstake.com/shredstream/quickstart) | gRPC x-token metadata, per subscription | Dashboard, self-serve
Direct Shreds (https://docs.blockspace.everstake.com/direct-shreds/quickstart) | Source-IP allowlist on a dedicated link | Dashboard, ~30 min provisioning
SWQOS (https://docs.blockspace.everstake.com/swqos/quickstart) | No token — open endpoint; tip transfer in the tx (HTTP) or QUIC keypair allowlist | Dashboard, self-serve (both HTTP and QUIC)
Relayer/TPU (https://docs.blockspace.everstake.com/mempool/quickstart) | Token + signing-pubkey allowlist, application-based | Application review
There is no single account-level "API key" that unlocks every product. Tokens and allowlists live next to the product they govern.

## Where to get credentials​
- Sign in to the dashboard (https://app.blockspace.everstake.one/).
- Subscribe (or apply, for application-gated products).
- Open the product page — the connection details (endpoint, token, region, allowlist form) are on that page.

## Rotating credentials​
Each product page has its own rotate flow. For token-based products, generate a new token, deploy it, then revoke the old one — both remain valid during the swap so there's no downtime.

sources.text:
On this page

# FAQ

## Access & Authentication​

### How do I authenticate?​
It depends on the product. ShredStream and Relayer/TPU use tokens; Direct Shreds uses source-IP allowlists; SWQOS HTTP is open with an on-chain tip; SWQOS QUIC uses a signing keypair. See Authentication (https://docs.blockspace.everstake.com/getting-started/authentication) for the full matrix.

### Can I share credentials across multiple servers or apps?​
For token-based products, the token is scoped to your subscription and can be used across as many backends, workers, or clients as you want. For allowlist-based products (Direct Shreds, SWQOS QUIC, Relayer/TPU), each source IP or signing pubkey needs to be listed explicitly.

### How do I rotate credentials without downtime?​
Generate a new token (or add a new IP/pubkey) in the dashboard (https://app.blockspace.everstake.one/), deploy it, then revoke the old one. Both stay valid during the swap so there's no gap.

## Plans & Billing​

### What payment methods are accepted?​
Card and crypto. Both are configured in the dashboard; crypto invoices settle in USDC on Solana or Ethereum.

### How do I upgrade or change plans?​
In the dashboard (https://app.blockspace.everstake.one/) → service page → Plan. Plan changes apply immediately; prorated billing on the next cycle.

## Products​

### Which chains are supported?​
Blockspace MEV products target Solana exclusively — that's where Everstake's validator stake translates directly into latency and inclusion advantage.
